title: Implement LRU Cache
question: Implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache. Requirements: 1) O(1) get and put operations, 2) Fixed capacity, 3) Thread-safe, 4) Evict least recently used when full. Discuss: using LinkedHashMap with accessOrder=true for built-in solution, or implementing custom solution with HashMap + doubly linked list, maintaining head (most recent) and tail (least recent) pointers, moving accessed nodes to head, removing tail node when capacity reached, implementing get() by looking up in HashMap and moving to head, implementing put() by adding new node at head and removing tail if needed, synchronizing methods for thread safety, considering ConcurrentHashMap with custom eviction for better concurrency, and testing with multiple threads.

title: Design HashMap from Scratch
question: Design and implement a HashMap from scratch. Requirements: 1) Support put, get, remove operations, 2) Handle collisions, 3) Dynamic resizing, 4) Good hash distribution. Discuss: creating array of buckets (LinkedList or Node array), implementing hash function (hashCode() % capacity), handling collisions with chaining (linked list in each bucket), implementing put() to calculate bucket index and add/update entry, implementing get() to find bucket and search through chain, implementing resizing when load factor exceeds threshold (0.75), rehashing all entries on resize, using prime number capacity for better distribution, implementing treeification for long chains (Java 8 optimization), handling null keys specially (index 0), and testing collision scenarios.

title: Find Top K Frequent Elements
question: Find top K frequent elements in a stream of data. Requirements: 1) Real-time processing, 2) Memory efficient, 3) Handle millions of elements, 4) Return top K at any time. Discuss: using HashMap to count frequencies, using MinHeap of size K to maintain top K elements, adding elements to heap and removing minimum when size exceeds K, using PriorityQueue with custom comparator for heap, considering Count-Min Sketch for memory efficiency with large datasets, using sliding window for recent frequencies, implementing with concurrent data structures for multi-threaded streams, using TreeMap for sorted frequencies with O(log n) updates, considering approximate algorithms (Heavy Hitters) for very large streams, and optimizing for query vs update tradeoffs.

title: Design Concurrent Counter

Design a thread-safe high-performance counter. Requirements: 1) Support for increment, decrement, get operations, 2) Handle high concurrency (1000+ threads), 3) Minimize contention, 4) Accurate count. Discuss: using AtomicLong for simple atomic counter, using LongAdder for better performance under high contention, understanding LongAdder's cell-based approach to reduce contention, comparing AtomicLong (single variable, CAS) vs LongAdder (multiple cells, striped), using DoubleAdder for floating-point counters, considering distributed counters for multiple JVMs, implementing sharded counter with multiple AtomicLong instances, using ThreadLocal for per-thread counting with periodic aggregation, benchmarking under different contention levels, and choosing based on read vs write ratio.
